answer.summary: Rauch described a tradeoff between withholding thinking tokens for competitive reasons—and uncertainty about their product value—and exposing them so users can understand and steer the AI. DeepSeek demonstrated that users valued the transparency, which also helped them identify mistakes.

sections.heading: The tradeoff
sections.content: Rauch said OpenAI had the technology but chose to withhold thinking tokens for competitive reasons; at the time, it was also unclear whether exposing them would provide end-user product utility. DeepSeek’s release made the upside clearer: users liked seeing how the AI thought and being able to influence its direction. Rauch also noted that visible reasoning could help users pinpoint where the AI went wrong and report it.
